title: Aggregate Borrower Exposure Across Home Mortgage Loans
content:
Mortgage exposure on Home Mortgage Loans is aggregated per borrower rather than judged loan by loan. The aggregate governs both the recording of a new application and the funding of a loan.

**The aggregate exposure limit.** The sum of the principal balance on the customer's active, delinquent and forbearance mortgage loans, plus the amount applied for, must not exceed $5000000.00.

The sum is taken from the bank's records of the customer's mortgage loans, correlated to that customer, and is taken before the application is recorded and again before the loan funds. A loan standing in applied status is not in that set; the amount applied for enters the sum as its last term.

**Mortgage principal outside this product.** Mortgage principal is also the one lending balance that counts toward the Personal Checking relationship balance of those tiers whose terms take mortgage balances into account, on the basis the Personal Checking terms set. No pricing on Home Mortgage Loans depends on any other holding the customer has.

## Worked illustration on hypothetical figures

A hypothetical borrower's records show an active loan with a principal balance of $1200000.00, a second active loan at $800000.00, a loan in forbearance at $450000.00 and a loan paid off two years ago. The three loans in a counted status carry principal balances that together come to $2450000.00; the paid-off loan carries none.

Against that aggregate, an application for $2550000.00 brings the total to exactly $5000000.00. The limit is stated as a ceiling not to be exceeded, so a total equal to it is within the limit. An application for $2600000.00 would bring the total to $5050000.00, which exceeds $5000000.00.

## Points of judgement

The status set that decides which balances are summed here is active, delinquent and forbearance. A balance on a loan that has been paid off is not in the sum, and neither is one on a withdrawn application.
